classes.name: Stakeholder
classes.description: An entity that provides or receives value through the system or service being developed. Represented by organization or role.
extract_rules: Avoid personal names; prioritize organization names and role names (e.g., health center, contractor, user, positive patient, contact tracer)
Normalize the same concepts and use a single canonical label (e.g., 'user', 'general user', 'app user' → 'user'). Do not split by attributes (language, age, etc.)
Use official names for organizations (e.g., Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Expert Advisory Committee)
Express role names as singular, concise noun phrases that match the terminology definitions in the specification or glossary
Extract external platform providers as infrastructure providers only when API/infrastructure provision is explicitly stated
Extract from contexts near the source where it can be confirmed that the entity is involved in receiving or providing value (actions, responsibilities, notifications, consent, supervision, etc.)
prohibit_rules: Do not register abbreviations instead of official names. Do not extract partial names from the original text
Do not extract system components or technical elements (e.g., notification server, system, OS, API) as stakeholders
Do not extract product, device, or general software terms (e.g., smartphone, app, server, cloud) as stakeholders
Do not misidentify procedures, obligations, or operational descriptions (inquiry response, FAQ preparation, consent UI, etc.) as entities. Exclude if the entity is not clearly an organization or role
Prohibit splitting by attribute differences (e.g., treating 'users who use languages other than Japanese' as a separate stakeholder). Express attributes as properties when necessary

Do not extract names from project structure or deliberative bodies if their role or responsibility is not confirmed in the specification (prohibit extraction from lists of names, greetings, references, etc.)

classes.name: Value
classes.description: Represents the benefits or desired states that stakeholders gain through the system or service being developed
extract_rules: Express benefits, outcomes, and achieved states concisely as noun phrases (e.g., privacy protection / promotion of behavior change / rapid information transmission)
Prioritize extraction from locations in the original text that contain predicates indicating benefits such as 'become able to', 'lead to', 'prevent', 'support', etc.
Maintain associated metadata about the anticipated stakeholder (user / Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare / society as a whole, etc.) so that the benefit recipient can be linked in later stages
The extraction unit is the benefit itself. For sentences where benefit and means are mixed, extract only the benefit portion
prohibit_rules: Do not extract functions, means, components, or technologies (e.g., notification function, Bluetooth usage, diagnosis key, server, OS/API, RPI/TEK) as values
Do not extract procedures, actions, or processes (e.g., registration, transmission, verification, download, settings) as values
Do not extract SLO/SLA performance, availability, or operational regulations (e.g., uptime rate, response time, data disposal procedures, FAQ preparation) as values

Do not adopt abstract slogans alone where the beneficiary or benefit content is unclear (e.g., improved convenience, efficiency) as-is (only allowed when supported by benefit descriptions in the original text)
Do not extract descriptions that only indicate the provider's work purpose (operation, management, response, service desk, etc.) as values (when the beneficiary's state change is not specified)

classes.name: Vision
classes.description: A statement that concisely expresses the long-term ideal state that a company, business, or project aims to achieve
extract_rules: Prioritize descriptions containing words that express broad-scope future states such as 'society as a whole/citizens/public/infrastructure/trust/transparency/sustainability/dissemination/interoperability'
Express the vision concisely as a noun phrase (e.g., 'Establishment of a digital infrastructure based on transparency and trust')
For sentences with specific means (API/cloud/CDN, etc.), separate the means and extract only the desired state to be reached
prohibit_rules: Do not extract means, methods, or configurations (e.g., API connection, CDN utilization, cloud utilization, OS requirements) as vision (classify as IT/system requirements)
Do not extract short-term numerical targets or operational goals (e.g., recovery within 72 hours, uptime rate, performance values) as vision (classify as non-functional/operational requirements)
Do not extract explanations of individual functions, screen specifications, operational procedures, consent flows, etc. as vision
Do not make benefits (sense of security, prompt notification, etc.) into vision as-is
Do not treat descriptions limited to an individual organization, a single department, or a single function (without a broad social vision) as vision
Do not adopt abstract statements with slogans only where the entity and future state are unclear (only allowed when the scope of the vision can be confirmed in the original text)
Sentences describing specific operational, coordination, notification, registration, and other business activities (content that should be classified as business requirements)

classes.name: Concept
classes.description: A statement that concisely expresses the activity policy toward realizing the ideal (vision) of a company, business, or project
extract_rules: Express policy, principles, or philosophy as noun phrases
Confirm whether it is an action guideline for realizing the vision, and name it at an abstract level that does not delve into functional details or numerical KPIs

Prioritize cross-cutting principles such as privacy, consent, transparency, neutrality, interoperability, data sovereignty (example basis: anonymous identifiers, on-device matching, transparency assurance, open standards, domestic region operations)
prohibit_rules: Do not extract functions, procedures, screens, flows, configurations, or implementation details (e.g., notification screen transitions, aggregation specifications, API connection procedures, OS/CPU/memory, etc.) as concepts
Do not extract non-functional numerical targets or operational KPIs (e.g., recovery within 72 hours, uptime rate, concurrent connections) as concepts
Descriptions that specify specific business operations, procedures, or service provision (content that should be classified as business requirements)
Do not extract benefits themselves (sense of security, prompt notification, etc.) as concepts
Exclude sentences that only mention compliance with external regulations, and adopt sentences that show the core of the policy (what you want to achieve and how)
Exclude individual tasks, FAQ preparation, and other operational procedures and administrative obligations

classes.name: Business Requirement
classes.description: Descriptions of business requirements demanded of the system or service being developed
extract_rules: The description should be a noun phrase or a short sentence (ending with a noun), and it is desirable to include the elements of to whom, what, and why.
Target business service provision and operations, and prioritize those where the entities involved such as government agencies, users, and businesses are clear.
Exclude sentences composed only of abstract benefit words (security, safety, trust, efficiency, improved convenience, etc.).
Actively extract sentences that include business activities such as 'notification', 'registration', 'inquiry', 'coordination', 'decision support', 'operations', 'reception', etc.
When benefits (purposes) and means are mixed, separate the benefit side as business-requirement and the means side as system-requirement.
prohibit_rules: Sentences that only explain communication methods, configurations, or technical means (Bluetooth, TEK, RPI, server, cloud, API, encryption methods, etc.)
Abstract slogans (e.g., ensuring security, safety, and reliability; improving convenience; business efficiency, etc.) where the target or criteria are unclear
Sentences about UI components, screen layouts, operational procedures, and other design details
Sentences about performance, availability, uptime rate, response time, numerical targets, and other SLO/SLA
Vision-like descriptions such as organizational policies, visions, planning policies, and development guidelines
Mere lists of product names, technology names, or identifiers (e.g., Bluetooth, API Gateway, TEK, UUID, etc.)

classes.name: System Requirement
classes.description: Descriptions of technical specifications for the system or service being developed
extract_rules: Describe specific technical specifications as noun phrases (e.g., hardware/software/network configuration, encryption methods, logging methods, API specifications, specific values of design policies)

Include specific specifications related to system structure and communication methods such as cloud configuration, network layer, authentication methods, and encrypted communication as extraction targets.
Include non-functional requirement criteria (numerical values, configuration policies) such as performance, scalability, redundancy, and availability as extraction targets.
May include non-functional numerical criteria (e.g., response time, concurrent connections, uptime rate, RTO/RPO)
Include technical requirements related to security, testing, and quality assurance (e.g., vulnerability assessment, static analysis, dependency library inspection) as extraction targets.
Include technical constraints such as data retention, anonymization, privacy protection, log management, and access control as extraction targets.
When requirements are complex (e.g., on-device matching + 14-day retention), divide and extract into atomic technical specification units (method, period, configuration).
prohibit_rules: Business requirements, project purposes, conceptual policy-level descriptions (e.g., for the purpose of providing services)
Sentences involving business activities (notification, registration, inquiry, operations, decision support, etc.) where entities such as government, development vendors, and users are involved
Descriptions aimed at fulfilling service provision responsibilities or achieving social roles (content that should be classified as business requirements)
Explanations of stakeholders or organizational structure (e.g., contractor responsibilities, operational structure)
Sentences that only describe management procedures such as operations, maintenance, distribution, and updates
Abstract design philosophy or guidelines (e.g., ensuring transparency, improving reliability, etc.) that do not involve technical specifications

classes.name: System Component
classes.description: Descriptions of modules and libraries that make up the system or service being developed
extract_rules: Extract only basic design level components (e.g., hardware configuration, OS/runtime, cloud services, external SaaS, library groups, packaged software)
Express labels as noun phrases (singular, concise)
If a product name or version is included, extract it as-is (e.g., PostgreSQL, Red Hat Enterprise Linux)
prohibit_rules: Functional design level elements (e.g., XX function)
Screen design elements (e.g., XX screen)

Elements related to system or service management, operations, or development environments (e.g., 'monitoring', 'health monitoring', 'resource monitoring', 'test environment', 'maintenance environment', 'configuration management', 'diagnosis target')
System or service design methods, regulations, or business procedures
System or service benefits, purposes, or activity policies (e.g., 'efficiency', 'improved convenience', 'for the purpose of providing services', etc.)

classes.name: Business Goal
classes.description: A management objective that utilizes insights gained from data analysis
extract_rules: Express the impact on business such as management
prohibit_rules: The source text is a description unrelated to data analysis
It is an explanation of system or service functions or operations
Just a business policy or slogan (e.g., 'Promoting business efficiency')
Those where the relationship with analysis is not specified

classes.name: Analysis Goal
extract_rules: Concisely express the purpose
prohibit_rules: The source text is a description unrelated to data analysis
It is an explanation of system or service functions or operations
Policies unrelated to analysis

classes.name: Analysis Result
classes.description: A description that organizes the results of data analysis
extract_rules: Organize and summarize data analysis content, algorithms, and analysis results
prohibit_rules: The source text is a description unrelated to data analysis
It is an explanation of system or service functions or operations
General expressions that do not show numerical values or trends
Those that correspond to evaluation or conclusions (should be classified as evaluation)

classes.name: Dataset
classes.description: Descriptions of datasets used for data analysis
extract_rules: Concisely describe the overview and characteristics of the dataset
prohibit_rules: The source text is a description unrelated to data analysis
It is an explanation of system or service functions or operations
All data for migration or operations ('all data from the current system', etc.)
Just a data name lacking characteristics

classes.name: Evaluation Result
classes.description: Descriptions of conclusions obtained by comparing data analysis results with business objectives
extract_rules: Describe the applicability to business
prohibit_rules: The source text is a description unrelated to data analysis
It is an explanation of system or service functions or operations
Descriptions of operational obligations, regulations, or policies (e.g., 'Periodic security assessments are required')
Just analysis results (should be classified as analysis-result)

properties.name: hasValue
properties.description: Associates the value that a stakeholder gains
prohibit_rules: The relationship is not explicitly stated in the text (there is no explicit statement that the Stakeholder receives/enjoys the Value)

The Stakeholder is in the position of provider, operator, administrator, service desk, or secretariat of the Value and does not enjoy the Value. Do not exclude if any of the following can be confirmed in the original text: (a) dest (Value) represents public benefit or 'organizational attainment state/benefit' such as organizational mission/achievement/KPI/regulatory compliance/reputation/financial soundness, etc., (b) src bears responsibility/purpose/evaluation (word examples: achievement, realization, evaluation indicator, KPI, achievement, mission, purpose, accountability, legal compliance, trust, reputation, cost-effectiveness, penalty avoidance, etc.) for achieving or maintaining that dest, (c) secondary benefits that src enjoys through provision activities (maintaining trust, achieving supervisory responsibilities, cost reduction, etc.) are explicitly stated as causation
dest refers to means, procedures, obligations, or components rather than benefits (e.g., implementing settings, applications, reports, disposal, etc.)

properties.name: hasBusinessRequirement
properties.description: Associates business requirements linked to value

properties.name: realizesValue
properties.description: Associates the value that the concept realizes

properties.name: hasSystemRequirement
properties.description: Associates system requirements linked to business requirements

properties.name: allocatedToComponent
properties.description: Associates the component to which the system requirement is allocated

properties.name: hasDataMiningObjective
properties.description: Associates data analysis objectives linked to business goals
prohibit_rules: There is no purpose clause in the original text (e.g., 'analyze XX for ~', 'perform XX analysis to achieve ~', etc.) (causation/purpose is not specified)
The analysis-goal is merely a list of functions/tasks, with no purposeful connection to the business-goal (e.g., just 'perform log management/analysis' without 'for the purpose of ~')
The business-goal is only an abstract slogan (e.g., 'promoting efficiency', etc.), and the causal clause with the analysis-goal is missing
The description is limited to general associations, and specific targets, means, or results are not shown (only ambiguous expressions such as 'analysis useful for ~', etc.)

dest (analysis-goal) refers to analysis results, evaluations, or implementation of measures (e.g., 'evaluation of impact', 'decision to correct', etc. results/measures are handled by separate properties)

properties.name: hasDataMiningResult
properties.description: Associates analysis results linked to data analysis objectives
prohibit_rules: The original text only describes analytical activities such as 'analyze ~', 'conduct analysis', 'target for analysis', and does not mention specific results or findings (revealed, identified, calculated, etc.)
dest is a decision, evaluation, or measure (e.g., decision, approval, documentation, improvement proposal, presentation of options) and is not the result of the analysis itself
Even if numerical values or indicators are shown, it is not explicitly stated in the original text that they were derived as a result of that analysis-goal (possibly due to another goal)
The description remains general or explanatory, and specific outputs (indicators/conclusions/classifications/correlations/impact/scope/causal estimation, etc.) are not shown
dest is a list of work procedures, operations, or requirements and does not represent analysis output

properties.name: usesDataset
properties.description: Associates the dataset used in the analysis results

properties.name: hasEvaluationResult
properties.description: Associates evaluation results for analysis results
prohibit_rules: src (analysis-result) is only a description of analytical activity and does not show specific results (revealed, identified, calculated, etc.)

src represents decision-making, evaluation, or planning (e.g., decision, approval, documentation, presentation of options, etc.) and is inappropriate as analysis-result (these are treated as evaluation)
The causal relationship with dest (evaluation) is not explicitly stated in the text (e.g., no 'based on ~', 'in light of ~', 'as a result of ~', etc.)
The justification remains general, and it cannot be confirmed that src actually contributed to the evaluation of dest
Even if src is a numerical value or indicator, it cannot be confirmed in the original text that decisions or policy settings were made based on the evaluation results (unattributed)
